open_points.subject: Function file ports with cardinality `many`
open_points.text: A03 rule 3: "A `file` port carries `bytes`." A03 rule 5: "...or a file output is not `bytes` — `contract_violation`..." A13 rule 6: "A `many` file port carries a list of files; inside the sandbox it is a list of `bytes` (A03)."
open_points.question: For function execution, what exact Python shape is required for `file` inputs/outputs when `cardinality` is `many`, and how is output validation applied?
options: All `file` ports must be `bytes` regardless of cardinality (so `many` file ports are effectively invalid)
Disallow `cardinality: many` on `file` ports at contract/proof time
open_points.default_guess: `file`+`many` should be `list[bytes]`, and validator should check list type plus each element is bytes.

open_points.subject: Operation binding file output cardinality
open_points.text: M01 allows `cardinality: one | many` for any port; A09 rule 3 says "A binding with a `file` output has no other output port ... and the body is that file".
open_points.question: Is a binding file output allowed to be `many`, and if not, where is it refused?
options: Restrict binding file outputs to `cardinality: one` only
Allow `many` and define response encoding/decoding for multiple files
Allow `many` only for internal flow typing but map service response to one file anyway
open_points.default_guess: Refuse binding proposals with `file` output cardinality `many`.

open_points.subject: `try implementation` on an empty corpus
open_points.text: A04 rule 6: "Trying an implementation ... executes ... the cases ... all of them when it names none ... records one TrialExecution per case and returns them." No rule says what happens when there are zero cases.
open_points.question: Should `try implementation` with no trial cases return an empty evidence set or be refused?
options: Refuse with a specific reason (e.g., empty corpus)
Refuse with the same refusal style as admission
open_points.default_guess: Return an empty TrialExecution list (no refusal).

open_points.subject: Owner access to spooled file bytes during approval
open_points.text: A10 rule 2: "The owner may read the spooled file's bytes through inspection while the run holds them."
open_points.question: Which inspect call identifies a specific spooled file and what limits/format apply to returning those bytes?
options: Add a dedicated inspect-by-file-handle operation with bounded streaming/chunking
Inline file bytes in existing run/trace inspection responses
Allow only metadata in inspect; no direct byte read despite this sentence
open_points.default_guess: Provide a dedicated bounded file-read inspect path keyed by run/node/map/attempt/port.

open_points.subject: Downstream scheduling from mapped nodes with partial completion
open_points.text: A13 rule 2: "A mapped node, once selected, runs every element it can in list order ... an element that waits does not stop the elements after it." Also: "a node is ready when every input port holds its value."
open_points.question: Can downstream nodes start from partial mapped outputs (for finished elements), or only after the mapped node has concluded all elements and produced full `many` outputs?
options: Downstream waits for full mapped-node completion (full list materialized)
Downstream may run per-element as soon as that element is available
Policy depends on consumer node kind/cardinality
open_points.default_guess: Downstream should wait until the mapped node concludes and full list outputs exist.
